answer.description: The submitted answer object; its shape follows the answer type and mode, and all text values are markdown. Null when the question was not answered.

answerMode.description: The layout of the answer: single, fielded, open, grid, or sectioned.

answerType.description: The answer type of the question: text or table.

filingID.description: The filing the answer belongs to.

gap.description: True when the question counts as a gap in the filing's completion.

id.description: The unique identifier of the filing question, formed from the filing id and the question id.

label.description: The reviewer's label for the answer: complete, partially_complete, or incomplete; null when unlabelled.

questionID.description: The question id within the filing schema (e.g. q1).

questionIndex.description: Zero-based position of the question within its section.

questionLabel.description: The question as shown to the filer.

schemaID.description: The identifier of the filing schema the question belongs to.

sectionIndex.description: Zero-based position of the question's section in the schema.

sectionName.description: The name of the schema section the question belongs to.

filingType.description: The filing type the schema applies to (e.g. B1, B2).

questionCount.description: Number of questions across all sections.

schemaID.description: The unique identifier of the filing schema.

sections.description: The schema's sections in order, each with its name and questions: id, label, answer type, configuration and instructions.

bwProjectID.description: The Blockworks research project id the filing belongs to.

bwProjectSlug.description: The Blockworks research project slug, used to group filings by project and in the filing's static URL.

completionLabel.description: Completion label derived from the gap count: complete, or partial with the number of gaps.

dateFiled.description: The UTC date the filing was published.

filingID.description: The unique identifier of the filing.

filingStatus.description: current, or stale when the filing is superseded or past its staleness deadline.

filingTypeRank.description: Rank of the filing among the project's filings of the same type, newest first; 1 is the latest.

filingVersion.description: The version of the filing schema the filing was answered against (e.g. 2.0).

gapCount.description: Number of questions with a gap: unanswered, unscored, or scored below complete.

isLatestForType.description: True for the newest filing of each type per project; filter on it to get one filing per type.

isSuperseded.description: True when a newer filing of the same type exists for the project.

projectID.description: The identifier of the mapped project record, when the research project is mapped to one.

projectName.description: The name of the mapped project record, when the research project is mapped to one.

projectSlug.description: The project's slug elsewhere in the API, when the research project is mapped to a project record.

protocolTicker.description: The asset ticker of the project's protocol; null when the project has no asset.

provenance.description: Who compiled the filing: issuer-filed or blockworks-compiled.

publishAt.description: When the filing was published, in UTC.

questionCount.description: Number of questions in the filing's schema.

stalenessTTLMonths.description: Months after the filing date before the filing goes stale, for filing types governed by a time-to-live rule.

staticURL.description: The public URL of the filing on blockworks.com.

submissionRound.description: The submission round that was published.

info.description: The Blockworks Data API is a unified, read-only REST interface to Blockworks' warehouse-modeled crypto dataset, powered by Messari's research and data infrastructure. It serves two kinds of models: tabular models, which return current, filterable, sortable rows for entities such as assets, networks, protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, and ETFs; and timeseries models, which return historical metric series at a chosen granularity for one or many entities. Every endpoint shares the same query grammar (column projection, per-column filters, sorting, and pagination) and returns the standard `{ "error": ..., "data": ... }` envelope. Authenticate by sending your API key in the `X-Blockworks-API-Key` header.
info.title: Blockworks Data API

parameters.description: Data granularity.
parameters.name: granularity

parameters.description: Comma-separated Currency values naming the series to return (up to 10). Omit it to get every Currency as a series in one response.
parameters.name: series

parameters.description: Time window, one of: to-date (ytd, qtd, mtd, dtd, htd); relative, <n> followed by m, h, d or w (30d, 12h, 4w; 1y and 1M are not accepted, use 365d, 52w, ytd or a calendar year); a calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD), month (YYYY-MM) or year (YYYY); or an RFC3339 instant, which runs from then to now. Mutually exclusive with start/end. parameters.name: timeframe

parameters.description: Window start, inclusive (RFC3339, unix seconds, or YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to the beginning of the data.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: Window end, exclusive (RFC3339, unix seconds, or YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to now.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: If true, return only the first and last point of the resolved time window instead of every point in it. A bounds request is exempt from the 9000-point maximum, since it returns at most two points per series however wide the window is.
parameters.name: bounds

parameters.description: Comma-separated metric fields to return; defaults to every metric. A point always leads with its timestamp, and the values that follow are described by point_schema in catalog order regardless of the order requested here.
parameters.name: selections

parameters.description: Response format, overriding the Accept header: json (default), csv, or jsonl (NDJSON). csv and jsonl return the rows as a downloadable file.
parameters.name: acceptFormat
